steps.label: Leakage warning
steps.pseudocode: A random split can leak the future into training.
steps.python:
n = 1000
customers = [{'id': i, 'week': i // 50 + 1} for i in range(n)]
train = [c for c in customers if c['week'] <= 14]
valid = [c for c in customers if 15 <= c['week'] <= 17]
test = [c for c in customers if c['week'] >= 18]
shuffled = [customers[(i * 37) % n] for i in range(n)]
r_train, r_valid = shuffled[:700], shuffled[700:850]
newest = max(c['week'] for c in r_train)
print('random:', sum(c['week'] < newest for c in r_valid), ' chronological:', sum(c['week'] < max(t['week'] for t in train) for c in valid))
# prints: random: 144  chronological: 0

steps.label: The final split
steps.pseudocode: Verify sizes and that the sets do not overlap.
steps.python:
n = 1000
customers = [{'id': i, 'week': i // 50 + 1} for i in range(n)]
train = [c for c in customers if c['week'] <= 14]
valid = [c for c in customers if 15 <= c['week'] <= 17]
test = [c for c in customers if c['week'] >= 18]
ids = [{c['id'] for c in part} for part in (train, valid, test)]
print(len(train), len(valid), len(test), ' overlap:', len(ids[0] & ids[1]) + len(ids[0] & ids[2]) + len(ids[1] & ids[2]))
# prints: 700 150 150  overlap: 0
